segments.he: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת לֹא חוֹלְצוֹת וְלֹא מִתְיַיבְּמוֹת, לִגְזוֹר מִשּׁוּם שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת דְּעָלְמָא, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «It was necessary» to state this again here «according to» the opinion of «Rabbi Shimon. It might enter your mind to say: Since Rabbi Shimon said» that «two sisters may not perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage,» as the very fact that they require levirate marriage from the same man and stand to become rival wives to each other renders them forbidden, «we should issue» a rabbinic «decree» in this case as well. Although in this case only one of the sisters is eligible for levirate marriage, as the other is a forbidden relative, perhaps there should be a rabbinic decree prohibiting the yavam from marrying the permitted sister, «due to» the similarity to the case of «two sisters in general» who happen before him for levirate marriage. «This teaches us» that even Rabbi Shimon does not hold that there is a rabbinic decree in this case.
